characterization_methods.key_findings: P-70 pattern contains only γ-Fe(M) fcc reflections (no α-Fe(M)); FWHM of the (111) peak of P-70 = 0.289 (largest of the five samples, implying smallest average grain size).

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) / inverse pole figure (IPF) mapping

characterization_methods.key_findings: At 70 W, numerous unfused powder particles and pores are present on the surface; the P-70 surface is the roughest, annotated 'Lack of fusion' and 'Hole'.

P-70 exhibited ductile dimple fractures plus fractures caused by decohesion and internal cracks, with poor tensile performance due to numerous unfused powder particles (Fig. 13(a) panel was not supplied in the figure group).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai F30 scanning transmission electron microscope; plasma polishing sample preparation
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the SLM alloy (studied on P-110): dense dislocation tangles in austenite, uniformly dispersed nanoscale κ carbide with [011]γ∥[011]κ; no ferrite detected.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM samples prepared by plasma polishing
characterization_methods.purpose: Study dislocations, κ carbide and orientation relationships in the SLM-printed alloy
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM)/HRTEM (noted for the SLM alloy)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: P-70 exhibited ductile dimple fractures together with fractures caused by decohesion and internal cracks; it exhibited poor tensile performance owing to numerous unfused powder particles in the sample.

interfaces.interface_notes: Ferrite diffraction patterns were not detected in the SLM-printed alloy. The nanoscale κ carbide orientation relationship and its uniform dispersion were characterized by TEM (bright-field, SADP, dark-field and HRTEM) on the SLM alloy.
interfaces.phase_evolution: The PREP powder contains both γ-Fe(M) and α-Fe(M) phases (γ dominant); after SLM printing at every laser power the alloy comprises mainly the austenite phase with no α-Fe(M), because ferrite formation is suppressed by fast cooling during SLM.

phase_interfaces.coherence: Oriented (coherent) relationship [011]γ ∥ [011]κ reported by SADP; nano-sized κ carbide uniformly dispersed in the austenite matrix. (OR established by TEM of P-110, representative of the SLM alloy; P-70 similarly contains nano κ carbide per the conclusion.)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength, tensile strength, elongation (mechanical properties)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Spherical Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder (particle diameter 15–53 μm) PREP-prepared (Advanced Corporation for Materials and Equipment, PREP-22); composition by ICP-OES (wt%): Mn 29.95, Al 8.63, C 1.20, Ni 3.45, O 0.01, Fe Bal. Highly spherical, narrow particle-size distribution, low oxygen content, no hollow particles; median particle size D50 = 35.69 μm, Hall flowability 14 s/50 g.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (99.99% pure); oxygen content in forming chamber maintained below 300 ppm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Printed on SLM Solutions SLM280; laser power 70 W (laser energy density 58.33 J/mm³), scanning speed 750 mm/s, spot diameter 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.02 mm, hatch space 0.08 mm; substrate preheated to 200 °C; 67° rotation angle applied to each layer; two sample sizes (75×12×12 mm and 10×10×10 mm). Sample denoted P-70.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Suns universal testing machine; Reliant electronic extensometer; loading rate 1 mm/min
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile sample, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 12 engineering stress–strain curves; P-70 is the black curve, the lowest of the SLM curves but still plateauing above 1000 MPa and ending in an abrupt vertical fracture drop.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: microhardness tester, load 0.5 kg for 10 s; each value is the arithmetic mean of five measurement points
Archimedes principle (relative density); laser confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 900) for surface roughness

defects.type: unfused powder particles / lack of fusion

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Right-skewed histogram; tallest bar at the lowest few μm bins reaching just below the 16% fraction, long thin tail extending to ~44 μm

phases_present.morphology: nanoscale particles uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

precipitates.coherency: [011]γ ∥ [011]κ orientation relationship with austenite (established by SADP on the SLM alloy / P-110)
precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: SLM-printed P-70 consists predominantly of the austenite phase (γ-Fe(M), fcc) with a small amount of nano-sized κ carbide and no α-Fe(M) ferrite (ferrite formation suppressed by fast cooling during SLM). The transverse cross-section shows fine equiaxed grains with random orientation (no preferred crystallographic texture).

unmapped_findings: XRD (111) peak FWHM of the P-70 sample = 0.289 (largest among P-70/P-90/P-110/P-130/P-150), consistent with the smallest average grain size.
Reduction of area (Z) of the P-70 sample = 25.79% (from the mechanical-properties table in Fig. 14).
Relative density of the P-70 sample = 98.27%, the lowest of the five SLM samples (porosity 4.75%, the highest).
P-70 surface roughness Sa = 20.71 μm (roughest of the SLM samples); its 3D surface topography maximum height is 144.6 μm.

P-70 fractured by ductile dimple fracture plus fracture caused by decohesion and internal cracks; it showed poor tensile performance owing to numerous unfused powder particles (Fig. 13(a) panel itself was not supplied).
SEM surface morphology of P-70 (70 W) shows numerous unfused powder particles and pores annotated 'Lack of fusion' and 'Hole', making it the roughest surface of the series.

The small amount of nano-sized κ carbide with a [011]γ∥[011]κ orientation relationship and the absence of ferrite were experimentally established by TEM on the SLM alloy (measured on P-110), not specifically on P-70.
